title: Staleness-aware microbatch composer for streaming chat (KV pressure smoothing)
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Streaming chat workloads show spiky KV cache pressure and variable token arrival patterns that cause GPU slab fragmentation and tail latency spikes during prefix-heavy sessions. Current batching coalesces by age or session heuristics independently which leads to either higher latency for fresh turns or unnecessary KV duplication in batches.

Goal: Implement a staleness-aware microbatch composer that merges short-aged turns opportunistically while gating merges with a heartbeat-driven slot allocator to smooth KV pressure and minimize GPU slab fragmentation. The composer should be latency SLO-aware (target p90 <= 60ms extra overhead) while reducing per-token GPU memory growth and improving throughput on multi-tenant hosts.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Age-weighted merge: assign each inflight turn an age score and a diminishing merge weight so very fresh turns are prioritized for low-latency routing while slightly older short-turn items can be merged to fill microbatches.
- Heartbeat slot gating: maintain a lightweight per-session heartbeat that reserves ephemeral \"merge slots\" for a short window (e.g., 12-50ms) to allow sibling turns to be grouped without extending p99 latency.
- KV-slot aging & opportunistic compaction: track per-request KV-slot lifetimes and perform opportunistic compaction/eviction when KV fragmentation surpasses a GPU-slab threshold; prefer compaction during microbatch assembly to avoid extra GPU memory pressure outside batching windows.
- Tail coalescing to combat fragmentation: when GPU slab fragmentation is detected, perform tail coalescing of microbatches (combine several small microbatches into a single packing operation) to improve contiguous memory usage and reduce allocator churn.
- Latency SLO gating: model expected extra scheduling delay caused by merge windows; if model predicts SLO breach for a turn, bypass merge and route to low-latency fast-path.

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end token-generation latency change <= +8ms; p99 change <= +20ms for streaming chat compared to current baseline.
- Throughput: Multi-tenant throughput improvement >= 6% across synthetic mix (chat-heavy workloads with 60:40 short:long turns).
- GPU memory: peak per-GPU slab usage reduced by >= 10% on high-churn hosts, and fragmentation score (measured by free-contiguous-bytes / total-free-bytes) improved by >= 15%.
- Stability: no regressions in streaming correctness or hallucination rate.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Simulation & validation (1 sprint): build a trace replay simulator that models arrival times, turn lengths, KV-slot lifetimes, and allocator fragmentation. Validate heuristics offline against synthetic and anonymized production traces.
2) Runtime prototype (2 sprints): integrate composer into batch planner as an optional gating policy behind a runtime flag. Instrument fine-grained metrics (merge_rate, bypass_rate, kv_compactions, slab_coalesce_events).
3) Canary & rollout (1 sprint): run in Dedicated canary (low percentage) with telemetry dashboards and automated rollback triggers.
4) Ramp & tune (2 sprints): observe production, adjust age-decay constants, heartbeat window, and compaction thresholds.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Waiting for merges can increase latency for some requests; mitigated by SLO gating and conservative defaults.
- Additional bookkeeping (heartbeats, KV-slot tracking) increases CPU and memory overhead; plan to implement lightweight structures and offload heavy bookkeeping to sampling.
- Compaction operations may introduce transient CPU/GPU overhead; schedule compaction during microbatch assembly where possible.

Instrumentation & observability:
- New metrics: composer.merge_window_ms, composer.merge_success_rate, composer.bypass_due_to_slo, composer.kv_compaction_count, composer.slab_coalesce_count, composer.avg_batch_fill_ratio.
- Dashboards: create a \"Composer Health\" dashboard with per-cluster and per-model breakdowns, and set alerts when bypass_due_to_slo > 5% or slab_coalesce_count spikes 3x baseline.

Docs / artifacts:
- Simulation harness: https://git.internal.redwood/sim/kv-batch-sim (WIP)
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Staleness-aware+Microbatch+Composer
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/221
- Initial runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7214

Rollout criteria for broader enablement: stable canary for 72h, no p95 regressions >2ms, merge_success_rate > 30% on chat traffic, and GPU slab fragmentation improvement observed on >50% of targeted hosts.
